title: Push, Pop, Parallelize: Stack-Augmented Linear Attention via the Delta Rule
claim: Our augmented model keeps lower per-token loss than the baseline as sequences extend beyond the training context length.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared legend below, dotted train-context marker
description: Two side-by-side line charts share one legend at the bottom. The left panel is CodeParrot and the right is OpenThoughts 114K Math. The x-axis is token position, from 1K to about 16K. The y-axis is token loss. Each panel has three noisy curves: dark blue for DeltaNet, light blue for DeltaStack with 8, and green for DeltaStack with 16. A vertical dotted gray line marks the 4K training context. In CodeParrot, DeltaNet sits clearly above both DeltaStack variants across all positions, and the gap holds well past the training context. In the Math panel, the three curves are close at first. DeltaNet then rises above the others, and loss grows with position for every model. The eye goes first to the separation between the dark blue line and the lower curves.
caption: Length Extrapolation on Reasoning Benchmarks. Per-token loss for 340M models trained on 15B tokens with 4096 context
abstract: Linear attention architectures based on the Delta rule, such as DeltaNet and RWKV-7, combine Transformer-level performance with RNN-like efficiency and provably solve regular language tasks. However, their fixed-size states struggle to capture the recursive, hierarchical structures intrinsic to natural languages. To bridge this gap, we introduce DeltaStack, which augments DeltaNet's associative memory with a lightweight, differentiable stack. Unlike prior approaches that rely on sequential recurrence, DeltaStack formulates stack operations as linear delta-rule updates, enabling a hardware-aware implementation fully parallelizable over sequence length. Theoretically, we prove DeltaStack extends DeltaNet's expressivity to model both regular and hierarchical languages. Empirically, DeltaStack outperforms DeltaNet and Stack-Attention on formal language benchmarks and consistently surpasses DeltaNet baselines in language modeling perplexity and zero-shot performance across scales up to 760M parameters. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/teeann/DeltaStack.
